segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, the E can split to IE. That's something we need to know about the present and it's something we need to be on top of. Now, it's in the present that this happens because, as we know, one of the fundamental elements of the present tense is to have that accent on the penultimate syllable. So, it's having that accent on the penultimate syllable that makes that E vulnerable to splitting. The E might split to IE or the O might split to UE. We know this already, actually, because we have puedo and this is a split O. "To be able", or "to can", of course there is no "to can" in English, "to be able" we say, is poder.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Here actually you can see closer that connection with "power". Before, I said that the word is related to the word "power" in English. El poder. El is the masculine "the", we also saw it's the word for "he", it's also the word for "the" for masculine words. El poder is "the power".

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So here it's a noun. It looks like a verb, but if it has "the" in front of it, we know it's a noun. El poder, the power. Poder, to be able.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: When you take off your ending and you change it for present tense and you stress that O, it splits into UE and you get puedo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Again, we can see the same phenomenon happening between words in English and Spanish. So, for example, we have the word "port" in English, but we say Puerto Rico.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Puerto Rico means "the rich port". Rico means rich or nice or tasty or sweet. So "port" becomes puerto. We see the O is splitting into UE.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We have the word "force" in English. In Spanish, this is fuerza.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We have the word "school". In Spanish, this is escuela.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We have "corp", in like "corporate", which means body. If "corp" means body in corporate, how do you think it is in Spanish?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We have "innovative", and this "nov" in "innovative" means new. When you do something innovative, you do something new. And the word for "new" in Spanish is nuevo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So you saw the O splitting there. You might have heard pueblo before. Pueblo means a village or a people.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: "Population" in Spanish is one of these exceptions. It's not populación, it's población. Población. And you can see the connection between población, población, and pueblo, which means village or people, a people. You can see the O in pob splitting to UE in pueblo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: "Mortgage", by the way, actually means "death pact". You have "mort-", which is the Latin root for death, and "gage", which means pact. And the word for "dead" in Spanish is, have a guess.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Well, actually here one, you have the noun: la muerte is "the death". So the noun is the word you put "the" in front of. In school, they tell you that it's the the thing, the object, but this is not an object. We will think of it, we put "the" in front of it, it's a noun: la muerte. But then the adjective which is describing is muerto or muerta, or muertos or muertas.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So you can see in those words between English and Spanish this phenomenon of this O splitting into UE when it takes the stress.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So this is useful for us for present tense. We need to know this for present tense, because if we have a verb like dormir, for example, that has an O in the root, when we stress it, it might split.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Something useful to bear in mind is that different versions of the verb, either the "to" form or some other version, might be the noun. So you mustn't assume always that it's a verb. If you see un encuentro, an encounter, this is now a noun, an encounter. Whatever we can put "a" or "the" in front of is a noun. So many times, some version of the verb will be the noun. Un encuentro is an encounter, but encuentro, I encounter.
